newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks slip as buyers turn cautious.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks slip as buyers turn cautious.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on Wednesday after buyers became cautious following the fatal shooting of a ruling party member of parliament the previous day, brokers said.

The all share index closed 2.62 points down at 618.24. Price falls outnumbered gains by 34 to 17. Highly capitalised blue chip Hatton Nantional Bank fell eight rupees to 247 and Merchant Bank one to 25.25.
"Buyers would not be unduly put off by Tuesday's incident, but will move to the sidelines to see if retail investors will panic and bring the index down," said a broker at John Keells.
Nalanda Ellawela, a member of the ruling People's Alliance, was shot by an unidentified gunman a day before nominations for local government polls were due to close.
Turnover was 24.6 million rupees on 1.5 million shares, led by foreign buying of Lion Brewery Ltd and Merchant Bank. Foreign buying amounted to 12.5 million rupees, while selling was 7 million.

"There were foreign day orders, but it all depended on whether you could source quantities at slight discounts to market prices," said Gordon Nadesan, a trader at CT Smith Stock Brokers. -- Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319.
